definition: The series of elementary steps by which a reaction happens. The steps must add up to the overall equation and agree with the experimental rate equation.
A single event in a reaction mechanism: one collision between particles, or one particle breaking apart or rearranging.

The slowest step in a reaction mechanism, with the largest activation energy. It controls the overall rate, and its reactants (or those that form them in earlier fast steps) appear in the rate equation.
A species formed in one step of a mechanism and used up in a later step, so it is not in the overall equation. It is a real species and sits in a dip (a minimum) on the energy profile.

The highest-energy arrangement of atoms in an elementary step, with bonds partly broken and partly formed. It sits at a peak of the energy profile and cannot be isolated. Also called the activated complex.
The number of reacting particles taking part in one elementary step: unimolecular (one), bimolecular (two) or termolecular (three, rare).
